summary: Dune (2019 Gale Force Nine edition of the 1979 classic) is a sprawling negotiation game where six asymmetric factions scheme, ally, and betray each other over control of Arrakis's spice. Most of the game happens in the talking phase between turns, where players cut deals, trade cards, and plan betrayals before a comparatively simple battle resolution plays out.
praised: Strong faction asymmetry that changes strategy each game
Iconic theme execution tied closely to the novel
High player interaction and memorable table stories
criticised: Long playtime, especially first games (3+ hours)
Kingmaking and alliance politics can frustrate players who feel shut out
Steep rules overhead and asymmetric onboarding for new players
Downtime when not directly involved in a negotiation

interaction.kind: secret alliances, betrayal, and bidding/bribery over the same board and spice
interaction.detail: Players negotiate treachery cards, alliances, and troop movements directly with each other every turn, and the entire game revolves around a shared map and shared spice supply that everyone fights and bargains over. Good moves are frequently chosen specifically to deny or manipulate another faction, and alliances can flip mid-game.
interaction.said: Widely called the archetypal negotiation game — reviewers describe constant secret alliances, backstabbing, and 'you must ally or die'; often cited as 'the best negotiation game ever made'

scoring.how_you_win: A faction wins instantly by holding 3 of the 5 strongholds at the start of a Spice Blow/Nexus phase; if turn 10 ends with no such win, the Spacing Guild (or a faction with a correct secret prediction) wins alone instead.

similar: Rex: Final Days of an Empire

theme.said: widely called 'the best simulation of a novel via mechanics,' 'the theme and rules are inseparable,' rarely if ever described as pasted-on
theme.why: the storm crossing the desert, the sandworm devouring spice and troops in the open desert, Bene Gesserit's secret prediction of the winning faction and turn, and the Atreides player alone knowing the traitors are all mechanics lifted directly from specific plot devices in the book

style.said: dudes on a map / thematic negotiation wargame
style.why: Wildly asymmetric factions battle, bluff, and betray each other over territory with combat resolved by cards and dice, and the narrative of alliances and treachery matters as much as efficiency
